steps.text: here's something you already do: you talk to yourself. all day. planning, remembering, wondering, commenting.
that voice is made of words. and the words you use quietly shape what you notice, what you want, and who you think you are.

steps.prompt: here's the same day, said three ways. just notice how each one lands.
options: today was a lot, and i got through it.
steps.question: which one sounds most like you today?
steps.reply: none of them is better. they're just different lenses on the same day.

steps.prompt: one more. you're heading to work.
options: i have to go to work.
i'm choosing to go to work, because i want the paycheck.
steps.question: notice a difference?
steps.reply: any of those is okay. the more you play with words, the more you'll notice.

steps.text: you're not doing anything wrong. your words have been doing a lot of work for you, for a long time.
hey you is a place to see how your words work, and to collect more of them. more ways to say what's true. more room to be yourself.

steps.prompt: three things you can explore here, in any order:

items.name: words
items.text: how you talk to yourself, and new ways to try

items.name: wants
items.text: what you actually like, outside of everyone else

items.name: thoughts
items.text: what you actually think, and saying it

steps.text: everything you discover lands in one place: me, collected. a picture of you, in your own words. it stays on this phone.

items: no streaks, ever. come back whenever you want.
this isn't therapy, and you never have to share anything you don't want to.

steps.prompt: let's start your collection. what's one thing you like? anything at all.

steps.text: that's the first piece of you, collected. welcome.

grounding.idea: putting experiences into words can change how intense they feel
a clearer sense of who you are is linked to wellbeing
